clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Spectral clustering on NPMs to derive subtypes; anatomical separability via SVM AUC with cross-validation; Spearman correlations between atypicality indices (overall and regional) and clinical measures (ADOS-2, ADI-R, SRS-2, RBS-R, SSP) and ADHD ratings; associations with polygenic scores; multiple comparisons controlled (FDR).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Five neuroanatomical subtypes of ASD emerged (three with decreased CT, two with increased CT), showed anatomical separability, and related more strongly and differentially to symptoms and polygenic risk than case–control approaches.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Spectral clustering of vertex-wise deviation maps (NPMs) in 316 ASD participants yielded five clusters. SVM-based separability achieved significant pairwise AUCs (P<0.0001, permutation). Clusters exhibited distinct patterns of increased/decreased cortical thickness and differential associations with clinical measures; atypicality indices correlated with multiple symptom scales and polygenic scores (some surviving FDR). These results suggest that subgrouping by normative deviations reveals stronger clinical and genetic associations than pooled case–control analyses.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Large amounts of missing clinical/behavioral data reduced power; genetic analyses underpowered; potential non-random missingness; no manual FreeSurfer edits (eliminates operator bias but may reduce reconstruction quality in some cases).
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Normative modeling with GPR trained on NT; site and image quality covariates included; extensive resampling for cluster stability and separability; scikit-learn used for SVM and clustering; acquisition harmonized using ADNI-like protocol.

general_notes.general_notes: NT cohort excluded individuals with intellectual disability for normative reference. T1 acquisitions matched to ADNI protocol across sites. Cortical surfaces smoothed with 10-mm kernel. Clustering used cosine similarity and 10,000 random initializations with inertia minimization.
